label: FY2027 Q1 (Jul–Sep 2026)
asOf: close of $30.44 on 2 Nov 2026 (Nasdaq.com); higher after hours on 3 Nov
headline: $20B of sales and $1.6B of profit in one quarter, for a market value of just $23B: the market doesn't believe Supermicro can keep its margins, or turn profit into cash

points.b: Revenue up fourfold in a year
points.t: Revenue of $19.95B, against $5.0B a year ago and $11.1B last quarter; Q2 guidance is $19.5–21.5B and FY27 $72–82B.
Last quarter's 17.5% was an outlier; this quarter 12.7%, with an operating margin of about 10%. In this business, gross margin swings with big customer orders.
Net income of $1.59B but operating cash flow of −$434M: receivables rose $3.6B and inventory $2.5B, only partly offset by $3.1B more in customer deposits.

reaction: Stock: closed at $30.44 before the report (2 Nov), down 7.6% that day, and rose after hours on 3 Nov (investingLive, Benzinga headlines). On 10 Jun the company announced a roughly $7B financing plan (including preferred stock) and the stock fell about 28% in a day; it jumped after the 20 Oct guidance raise. On 3 Nov it closed at $31.39 (+3.1%). Next day (4 Nov) it closed at $29.60, −5.7%, against −7.2% for the Dell/HPE average. 4 Nov was the first day after the midterms, when the AI chain split: cloud companies rose while power, cooling and construction stocks fell hard. Consensus from MarketBeat: EPS $1.23, revenue $17.53B; investingLive cites Q2 consensus of about $18B in revenue and $1.14 in EPS.

segments.title: Why profit didn't become cash
segments.bridgeT: From net income to operating cash flow
segments.take: It earned $1.59B, but customer payment terms and stock for next quarter absorbed $6B, and $3.1B of customer deposits offset only half of that.

rows.why: Servers and full racks with NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, mostly liquid-cooled. Customers are cloud companies, neoclouds and large enterprises. The company says it added several hundred enterprise customers over the past year but doesn't disclose its largest customers' shares.

Racks, liquid cooling, power, networking, software and field service sold as a package, “from gigawatt-scale data centers to single-container PODs”. The company treats it as its main lever for margins.

segments.note: This quarter's release has unaudited preliminary figures with no split by customer or product. Payables and other = accounts payable +$474M, accrued liabilities +$446M, income taxes payable +$223M, prepaid and other assets −$350M, and so on.

extras.title: Where it sits in the AI loop
extras.take: Supermicro is the loop's system assembler: it buys GPUs from NVIDIA and AMD and memory from Samsung and Micron, and builds servers and liquid-cooled racks for cloud companies. Revenue is huge, but most of it is pass-through chip cost; the gross margin it keeps is only 10–13%.

items.b: Speed of delivery is the pitch
items.w: Supermicro's edge is delivering liquid-cooled full racks fastest when a new GPU generation arrives. At this scale, delivery speed and capacity decide whether it wins big orders.
Gross margin jumped between 6.3% and 17.5% over the past five quarters. Big-order pricing, GPU and memory costs and one-offs all swing profit widely.
Inventory of $15.1B and receivables of $9.7B both rose sharply from last quarter. The more it sells, the more it must pay for GPUs up front.

It announced about $7B of financing in June (including preferred stock), and the balance sheet carries $4.67B of convertible notes and $4.0B of bank debt; it paid $64M of preferred dividends this quarter. Fully diluted shares rose from about 660M a year ago to about 770M.

Supermicro has a history of late filings and an auditor change, and the market has long given it a very low multiple. This quarter's figures are still “preliminary, unaudited” and may change before the formal 10-Q.

extras.title: Where growth comes from
extras.take: Supermicro's revenue follows GPU shipments: it assembles as much as NVIDIA and AMD deliver. The real variables are whether margins stabilize above 10% and whether working capital comes back.

items.w: The full-year midpoint of $77B is nearly double FY26. But the first half is already about $40B, so guidance implies about $18B a quarter in the second half, below the first half.
Opex is just 2.4% of revenue this quarter, so each point of gross margin moves operating profit by about $200M.
Only when receivables and inventory start falling will profit turn into cash. That is the key to whether Supermicro earns a higher valuation.
The company gave a full-year revenue range but no full-year margin or EPS.
Big customers delaying deliveries; GPU supply or price changes; gross margin back below 10%; the formal results differing materially from the preliminary figures; more equity or convertible issuance.

trends.why: 4x in a year, with big quarter-to-quarter swings

valuation.take: About 6.5 times trailing GAAP earnings, about 5 times our FY27 estimate, and a P/S of about 0.4, the cheapest company we cover and near the low end of its five-year range. It is cheap because margins are unstable, cash flow is negative, the share count is being diluted, and it has a governance history.

tiles.f: operating cash flow has swung between positive and negative over the past year, with no steady free cash flow

forward.title: FY2027 from company guidance
steps: Second-half revenue = $77B midpoint − $19.95B − $20.5B ≈ $36.6B, at a 7% operating margin, 21% tax and 769M shares ≈ $2.6
forward.note: The second-half margin is our assumption; the company gave only Q2 EPS and full-year revenue.

scenarios.note: Bear: AI server orders slow, a price war, and margins back to FY25 levels; base: modest revenue growth with margins near FY26; bull: a bigger DCBBS share and margins near this quarter's. EPS = revenue × operating margin × (1 − 21% tax) ÷ 790M shares. These assumptions are ours and are not forecasts.

pricezone.sub: FY28 EPS × our P/E; price at the 2 Nov close (the day before the report)
pricezone.why: The price is a little above the zone: buying at $30.44, the base case gains about 81% and the bear case loses about 47%, a reward/risk of about 1.7. At the $29 top of the zone the reward/risk is about 2; at the $25 low end, about 3.3. We give only 8–12x, below most hardware companies, because margins and cash flow are unstable; if working capital starts coming back and the formal results bring no surprises, the discount has room to narrow.
pricezone.note: Under review: this quarter's figures are unaudited and preliminary, and working capital hasn't come back yet; waiting for the formal 10-Q in mid-November.

history.title: Against its own past 5 years
history.sub: P/S (TTM revenue, diluted shares), quarter ends
history.note: About 0.4x now, the lowest band in five years, against a median of about 0.9x; it was about 5x at the March 2024 peak. Revenue multiplying while the stock didn't keep up is the main reason the P/S is so low. Shares are adjusted for the 10-for-1 split of 1 Oct 2024. We calculate it from SEC quarterly revenue, diluted shares and quarter-end closes.

cash.title: GAAP EPS
cash.note: Operating cash flow was −$434M this quarter against −$918M a year ago and +$747M last quarter. Customer deposits (deferred revenue) rose from $2.6B to $5.7B, the quarter's biggest source of cash. Cash fell $0.6B from last quarter.

calc: About 769M fully diluted shares (the company's Q2 non-GAAP guidance basis), market value ≈ $23.4B; about $22.8B on 749M GAAP diluted shares
Cash $6.90B; bank debt $3.98B and convertible notes $4.67B (converts already in the diluted count); preferred stock about $4.2B
Scenario EPS = revenue × operating margin × 79% ÷ 790M shares; price = EPS × multiple, rounded
Historical P/S = quarter-end close × diluted shares ÷ TTM revenue (SEC XBRL, split-adjusted)
valuation.next: Next report around early February 2027; before then, watch whether the formal 10-Q matches the preliminary figures.

changes.now: Raised to $18.5–19.5B on 20 Oct, actual $19.95B; Q2 $19.5–21.5B.

changes.before: In August: more than $60B of FY26 new orders and a record backlog.

changes.now: This quarter 12.7%; no separate gross margin guide for Q2.
Preferred stock issued in June; about 770M fully diluted shares.
